question.problem: Simplify the polynomial $3x^2-2-4x - 6x^2+18,$ giving your final answer in standard form.
question.worked_solution:
First, we collect like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-2-4x-6{x}^{2}+18 & = \\ 3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{2}-2+18-4x & = \\ (3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{2})+(-2+18)-4x & = \\ (3-6){x}^{2}+(-2+18)-4x & = \\ -3{x}^{2}+16-4x & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to express our polynomial in standard form. 

The highest exponent term is $-3x^2,$ followed by $-4x,$ and finally $16.$

So, the standard form of the polynomial is

$$
-3x^2-4x+16.
$$
